title: Official Regulations of the Padel Game
author: International Padel Federation (FIP)
notes: Official court dimensions: 10x20 m enclosed court, service line positioned 3.00 m from back wall (6.95 m from net), back wall 4.00 m total height (3.0 m glass + 1.0 m mesh), side wall glass/mesh steps, net height 0.88 m center and 0.92 m posts. Ball rebound specification: 135–145 cm bounce dropped from 2.54 m onto hard surface, establishing baseline coefficient of restitution (e ≈ 0.73–0.76). Wire mesh opening rules: 50x50 mm to 70.8 mm diagonal, 2–4 mm wire diameter.

title: Physics of ball impacts with rigid surfaces and walls
author: Cross, R.
publisher: Sports Engineering / American Journal of Physics
notes: Impact mechanics, normal/tangential velocity vectors, and coefficient of restitution (e ≈ 0.70–0.78 on rigid 10–12 mm tempered glass vs variable/lower e ≈ 0.35–0.55 on compliant wire mesh). Explains specular reflection on glass (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) and kinetic energy dissipation during ball-turf-wall collisions.

title: Análisis del golpe de doble pared abierta en pádel profesional: diferencias entre género
author: Sánchez-Alcaraz, B. J., Muñoz, D., Ramón-Llin, J., Siquier-Coll, J., & Courel-Ibáñez, J.
notes: Empirical match analysis of 451 double-wall shots across 20 professional matches, categorizing double walls with body turn/rotation (giro) versus without turn, ball trajectory directions (cross-court vs down the line), and tactical rally continuation efficacy.

title: Manual de Técnico de Pádel: Geometría de rebotes y táctica defensiva
author: Federación Española de Pádel (FEP) Coaching Committee
notes: Authoritative technical coaching framework distinguishing Doble Pared que Abre (side-to-back opening toward center court) requiring rotational pivot footwork from Doble Pared que Cierra (back-to-side closing into body/corner) requiring forward adjustment steps without over-spinning. Establishes the 'Pared-Jugador-Pelota' (Wall-Player-Ball) spatial positioning hierarchy.

title: Exploring offensive players' collective movements and positioning dynamics in high-performance padel matches using tracking technology
author: Ramón-Llin, J., Guzmán, J. F., Martínez-Gallego, R., Vučković, G., & Muñoz, D.
publisher: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport
notes: Computer vision tracking study establishing functional baseline defensive positioning: optimal sweet spot is 0.5–1.0 m behind the service line (2.0–2.5 m from the rear glass) and 1.0 m inward from the side wall, preserving operational radius and reaction windows.

title: Analysis of Off-The-Wall Smash Shots in Men’s and Women’s Professional Padel
author: Martín-Miguel, I., Muñoz, D., Escudero-Tena, A., & Sánchez-Alcaraz, B. J.
notes: Kinematic match analysis of off-the-wall shots (salida de pared and bajada de pared), showing incoming ball velocities of 40–100 km/h, rebound exit angles, contact point timing ahead of the body, and transition from defensive containment to aggressive counter-attack.

title: Padel an increasing cause of sport-related eye injuries in Sweden
author: Kasiga, T., & Bro, T.
notes: Ophthalmic epidemiology documenting padel as a leading cause of sports eye trauma (accounting for 20% of cases, escalating to #1 sport injury by 2021). Identifies padel ball diameter (6.35–6.77 cm) fitting within orbital socket aperture, causing hyphema, vitreous hemorrhage, and retinal detachment from close rebounds off mesh and glass.

title: Game performance and length of rally in professional padel players
author: Courel-Ibáñez, J., Sánchez-Alcaraz Martínez, B. J., & Cañas, J.
notes: Establishes that over 80% to 83% of padel points are won by net attackers, emphasizing the vital importance of defensive wall exits that neutralize pace rather than feeding high-speed chest-height balls to volleyers.

title: Analysis of game performance indicators during 2015–2019 World Padel Tour seasons and their influence on match outcome
author: Escudero-Tena, A., Sánchez-Alcaraz, B. J., García-Rubio, J., & Ibáñez, S. J.
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
notes: Demonstrates that unforced errors on baseline and corner wall shots are the primary statistical differentiator between winning and losing pairs; rushing strokes before wall rebounds multiplies error rates 4-fold.

title: Differences in shot selection and outcome between professional and recreational padel players
author: Martín-Miguel, I., Escudero-Tena, A., Muñoz, D., & Sánchez-Alcaraz, B. J.
publisher: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
notes: Contrasts amateur vs professional wall play: recreational players get jammed against back glass (<0.8 m), face the rear wall square rather than unit-turning sideways, swing with long tennis backswings, and back up toward the glass after the bounce.

title: Perception, Cognition, and Decision Training: The Quiet Eye in Action
author: Vickers, J. N.
notes: Explains visual interception mechanics, saccadic tracking, and Quiet Eye duration (300–450 ms fixation on projectile trajectory prior to initiation of interceptive swing) in fast ball-rebound sports.

title: Match analysis, physical demands, and injuries in padel players: a systematic review
author: Demeco, A., de Sire, A., Marotta, N., Spanò, R., Curci, C., Farì, G., Cioce, G., & Ammendolia, A.
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
notes: Systematic review of padel injuries: acute lower-limb trauma (inversion ankle sprains, meniscus and cruciate tears from sudden rotational pivots on sand-dressed turf) and knee patellofemoral overload from sustained low defensive crouches near perimeter walls.

title: Incidence of musculoskeletal injuries in amateur padel players: A prospective study
author: Castillo-Lozano, R., & Casuso-Holgado, M. J.
notes: Prospective epidemiological study reporting 3.0 to 8.0 injuries per 1,000 match hours in amateur players; identifies tripping while back-pedaling toward walls and collisions with perimeter structures as high-risk acute mechanisms.

title: Epidemiological study of injuries in padel players: analysis of injury mechanism and risk factors
author: García-Fernández, P., Guodemar-Pérez, J., Ruiz-López, M., et al.
publisher: Revista Iberoamericana de Ciencias de la Actividad Física y el Deporte
notes: Documents traumatic physical collisions with tempered glass panels and metal mesh enclosures, composite racket bounceback injuries off solid walls, and shoe-turf traction shear during sudden defensive direction changes.

title: Decision rules for the use of radiography in acute ankle injuries: refinement and prospective validation
author: Stiell, I. G., Greenberg, G. H., McKnight, R. D., et al.
notes: Defines Ottawa Ankle Rules for clinical triage of acute ligamentous tears and malleolar fractures resulting from foot inversion slips on sand-covered artificial turf near walls.
